idiom_name: branded minor-unit amount type with a currency type parameter
implementation_notes: TypeScript cannot change the runtime, so the pattern becomes a type-level discipline on top of JavaScript's BigInt integers: a branded type such as bigint & { readonly __brand: 'Cents' } makes the minor-unit amount distinct from every other number, a generic Money<C extends CurrencyCode> makes cross-currency arithmetic a compile error, and the only constructors are validated gates that check range or scale. Arithmetic wrappers (add, multiply, percentOf) replace the classic operator set and re-validate their results, while Intl.NumberFormat performs display from an exact decimal string. The classic mutable class is worth keeping only if a team wants method syntax; the type brand is what prevents the mistakes.
pitfalls: Brands are erased at runtime, so decoded JSON must be re-validated at the boundary rather than trusted because the type says Cents.
Number(bigint) or Math.round sneaks floats back in; percentage helpers must round half-even over integers instead.
An `as Cents` cast in application code defeats the scheme entirely, so the constructor has to be the only sanctioned entry point.
Settings that keep currencies closed at compile time only work while the currency set is a union type; config-driven currencies fall back to runtime checks.
